svg.title: Greedy Algorithms
svg.desc: Greedy Algorithms. Take the choice that looks best right now and never revisit it: optimal for some problems, quietly wrong for others. Step 1, Take the biggest that fits: Make 63 by always taking the largest coin that fits: 25, 25, 10, 1, 1, 1. Six coins, the fewest. Step 2, Greedy can be wrong: Coins 1, 3, 4 and amount 6: greedy takes 4, 1, 1, three coins, but 3 + 3 needs only two. Step 3, The right rule, proven: One room, nine requests: earliest start first books 1 meeting; earliest end first books 5, the most. Step 4, Greedy inside gzip: Huffman coding merges the two rarest symbols each time: abracadabra takes 23 bits instead of 33.

g.text: Make 63 by always taking the largest coin that fits: 25, 25, 10, 1, 1, 1. Six coins, the fewest.
Coins 1, 3, 4 and amount 6: greedy takes 4, 1, 1, three coins, but 3 + 3 needs only two.
One room, nine requests: earliest start first books 1 meeting; earliest end first books 5, the most.
Huffman coding merges the two rarest symbols each time: abracadabra takes 23 bits instead of 33.

g.text: These coins are canonical: greedy is
O(d log d + k): d coin types, k coins

Finishing first leaves the most room
for the rest: the exchange argument

a: 5 × 1 bit; b, r, c, d: 6 × 3 bits
